papers.title_en: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
papers.authors: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang, Jianming Ma, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen
papers.evidence: 智能体自撰文本记忆与精炼的工作记忆
papers.tldr: 当前具身智能体常依赖额外策略与自我改进框架，但其是否超越多模态大模型原生能力仍不清楚。SimplEvo不更新权重、无需特权信息，仅让模型从单次示范写入无坐标任务记忆，并在训练回合中构建和精炼有界工作记忆。在EBench上，GPT-6-Astra直接控制成功率从46.7%升至81.7%，RoboDojo达69.63%成功率与75.32分。该工作表明纯文本记忆演化即可显著释放MLLM的具身执行潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

papers.title_en: Joi-Bench-Task: Benchmarking Task Coordination in Full-duplex Voice Agents through Interactive Simulation
papers.authors: Xiangheng He, Mingjun Zhao, Zhehao Fan, Zhengjia Li, Xiaopeng Sun, Qingqing Xiao, Haolan Chen, Yu Xu
papers.evidence: 面向自主语音智能体任务协调能力的评测基准
papers.tldr: 全双工语音代理支持自然免提交互，但现有基准难以单独评估任务执行与对话协调。本文提出 Joi-Bench-Task，通过交互式用户模拟器在工具执行和语音结果交付的指定时点注入可控干预。评估五个商用语音代理发现持续协调失败：请求变更下最高完成率仅55%，五分之四代理中断后信息遗漏率至少23%。该工作将任务协调识别为复杂演进对话中的核心挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Full-duplex voice agents enable natural, hands-free interaction, allowing users to refine requests, redirect ongoing work, and seek clarification while the agent is speaking. However, existing voice-agent benchmarks insufficiently isolate coordination between task execution and conversation. We introduce a benchmark that assesses this coordination by examining whether agents track what is being executed, what has been completed, what has been communicated, and what remains to be reported as the conversation evolves. We propose an interactive user simulator that introduces configurable interventions at designated timing in tool execution and spoken result delivery, supporting controllable and reproducible evaluation conditions. We evaluate five leading commercial voice agents along three dimensions: execution responsiveness, coordination under request changes, and coordination under interruptions. Agent evaluations reveal persistent coordination failures. Under request changes, the highest result completion rate is only 55%, indicating difficulty for current voice agents adapting to new requests while preserving earlier obligations. After user interruption, four of the five agents exhibit average information omission rates of at least 23%. These findings highlight task coordination as a central challenge for current voice agents in complex, evolving conversations.

papers.title_en: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents
papers.authors: Loka Li, Duzhen Zhang, Xingbo Du, Leonard Song, Kun Zhang, Le Song
papers.evidence: 用于评测自主生物医学机器学习智能体的研究级基准
papers.tldr: 现有生物医学建模智能体基准规模小、接近饱和且存在信息泄漏风险。BioXArena-Pro 构建了覆盖8个生物医学领域的64项研究级建模任务，多数按物种或队列等完整生物单元留出测试。22种智能体配置中最高仅55.1分，且脚手架影响几乎与模型相当。该基准还通过重跑已发表方法揭示智能体在新数据上的适配优势，为自主生物医学建模提供严格评测。
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous builders of biomedical models, but existing benchmarks are small, near saturation or open to leaked information. We present BioXArena-Pro, 64 research-level modelling tasks from eight biomedical domains, each rebuilt from a published study; most hold out whole biological units such as species or cohorts. Across 22 agent configurations, the best scores 55.1 of 100, and the scaffold matters almost as much as the model. We re-ran a published method for every task: where the published recipe applies unchanged, the best agent and the methods tie; on rebuilt tasks the methods trail by 8.2 points, suggesting that agents gain by adapting to new data. Pretrained models (including biological foundation models) matter where the strongest agent uses them: forbidding them decreases its score on those tasks by 9 points. Every task was audited in several AI-assisted rounds and a final human review.

papers.title_en: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
papers.authors: Mingxi Zou, Yinghui Xu, Jiaxiang Chen, Langzhang Liang, Wei Zhu, Peng Ye, Runkai Zhao, Ruoxi Jiang, Sijin Chen, Song Wang, Zhuo Wang, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu
papers.evidence: 为大模型提供共享语义索引的解耦式长期记忆系统
papers.tldr: 语言模型不断迭代，但交互中积累的观察、修订与上下文仍需跨模型复用。MIGRO将长期记忆解耦为共享持久状态，采用“精确保存证据、近似组织、问题确定后再选择检索”的非对称保真与延迟选择策略，并用宿主接口适配不同模型的词表与分词。在LoCoMo匹配状态上答案质量提升7.3%、私有内存减少99.3%，跨模型交接后持续写入保留99.9%全历史重建质量，百万token BEAM历史平均私有存储减少57.5%。该工作实现了高质量、可增长且低存储的跨模型长期记忆。
papers.abstract_en: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that treats experience as a persistent state shared across successive language models.   MIGRO follows a simple principle: preserve historical evidence exactly, organize it approximately, and decide what to retrieve only when the question is known. We call this asymmetric fidelity with deferred selectivity. A shared semantic index supports retrieval, while exact records retain observations and their historical relationships. Because models differ in vocabulary and tokenization, host-specific interfaces convert selected evidence into inputs the receiving model can use. Reversible encoding reduces archival storage while enabling exact recovery. The shared state and its access interfaces let successive hosts read and extend the accumulated experience.   On matched LoCoMo states, MIGRO scores 7.3% higher and uses 99.3% less private memory than the strongest quality baseline. After handoff, continued writing retains 99.9% of full-history rebuilding quality by extending the inherited state. On million-token BEAM histories, MIGRO uses 57.5% less private storage on average than the most compact baseline. MIGRO combines high answer quality, continued memory growth across hosts, and low storage cost.   Code is available at https://github.com/zOUMINGXI/MIGRO.

papers.title_en: Publications as benchmarks: auditing AI agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment
papers.authors: Yiqun T. Chen, Jan Matthias, Jianing Yao, Hongyu Eric Zhao, Stephanie C. Hicks
papers.evidence: 将论文转化为可审计基准以评测AI智能体的框架
papers.tldr: AI代理正加速自动化数据分析，但在专业科学领域可靠评估成本高昂。作者提出将科学论文转化为可审计基准的框架，并在空间转录组对齐任务上测试121项任务、16个基线方法与6个AI代理。GPT-6-Astra与Gemini-4-Argon在80%任务上匹配或超越全部基线，且表现对提示和预装包不敏感。该工作还发现既往错误与指标捷径，并证明代理方案可蒸馏为可复用程序，为专业领域评估提供可扩展路径。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents are increasingly automating data analysis, but responsible adoption requires reliable performance evaluation, which is costly in specialized scientific domains. We introduce a framework that translates scientific publications into auditable benchmarks for AI agents and demonstrate its use on spatial transcriptomics alignment tasks. Across 121 tasks, 16 baseline methods, and six AI agents, the best agents (GPT-6-Astra and Gemini-4-Argon) matched or outperformed all baselines on 80% of tasks, often using surprisingly simple heuristics. Agent performance was robust to prompting and access to pre-installed packages. Benchmark construction also uncovered errors in prior work and shortcuts in current evaluation metrics. Finally, we show that agent-generated solutions can be distilled into a reusable program that ranks in the top 10% of baseline methods on unseen data. Our framework offers a scalable way to evaluate AI agents in specialized scientific domains by leveraging and stress-testing existing papers and metrics.

papers.title_en: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
papers.authors: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Xinwei Yang, Rongqing Li, Luyu Chen, Kieran Wong, Yudong Guo, Xinrui Wang, Jiayin Zhu, Pu Yao, Gu Simiu, Sulong Xu, Cong Fang
papers.evidence: 面向长程编码智能体的记忆控制训练
papers.tldr: 长程智能体的交互历史常超出上下文，因此需要自主决定何时写入、检索和复用记忆。已有在线策略蒸馏依赖模型预训练之外的记忆工具与压缩协议，导致教师难以指导、学生也难以采样到有效的记忆动作。作者提出CAMG-II长程环境套件与CAMP-II方法，借助Bash和持久工作区，通过全异步在线策略蒸馏，从具备文件操作先验的冻结教师那里学习文件式记忆。CAMP-II相较最强OPD基线增益达2.97倍，并迁移至Terminal-Bench 2.1和SWE-Bench Pro V2提升成功率。
papers.abstract_en: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual. Alongside each environment's native task interface, CAMG-II provides ordinary Bash access and an episode-persistent workspace, enabling the policy to create, revise, search, and reuse files as memory across context replacements. We also introduce Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II (CAMP-II), which trains a single policy jointly across all five environments with fully asynchronous OPD to learn this file-based memory behavior directly from a frozen teacher with a prior for file operations. On CAMG-II, CAMP-II obtains 2.97 times the gain of the strongest OPD baseline. The memory behavior CAMP-II learns generalizes to two external benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2, with improved success rates.

papers.title_en: PARLEY: Evaluating LLM Collaboration Through Cooperative Asymmetric Puzzles
papers.evidence: 用于评估大模型智能体协作的可扩展平台
papers.tldr: 大模型智能体协作研究缺少可扩展、可控制且贴近真实合作的任务平台。作者提出 PARLEY，以指称交流、联合协调、视角采择和空间推理四类非对称合作谜题评估 GPT-4o 智能体对。四百轮对话中平均成功率为百分之六十点五，任务间差异明显（百分之三十四至八十）。基于失败对话归纳出 PAC 分类法，并揭示反馈整合是失败关键，据此干预使平均成功率提升至百分之七十点五。
papers.abstract_en: As large language models power autonomous agents, understanding how they collaborate and where they fail becomes critical. We introduce PARLEY, an extensible platform for studying LLM agent collaboration through four asymmetric puzzle tasks grounded in cognitive psychology (referential communication, joint coordination, perspective-taking, and spatial reasoning). GPT-4o agent pairs succeeded in 60.5% of conversations (N=400, 100 per task), with task-level variation (34-80%) reflecting distinct collaborative demands. From these conversations, we derived the data-driven PAC taxonomy: six failure types organized into Perception (visual interpretation and spatial reasoning), Adaptation (progress tracking and feedback integration), and Coordination (verification and grounding). Failure to incorporate external feedback was a critical indicator of unsuccessful collaboration, with agents repeatedly applying unsuccessful strategies. We also show that a taxonomy-guided intervention (N=200) improved average task success to 70.5%. These results demonstrate how PARLEY can be used to derive meaningful, data-driven insights that can in turn lead to improved agentic collaboration.

papers.title_en: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
papers.authors: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown, Mihir Bhatia, Neelu Choudhary, Lily Miao
papers.evidence: 智能体评估框架及其稳定性的对比研究
papers.tldr: 企业分析型LLM智能体需可靠评估复杂多工具工作流。本文在冻结执行轨迹上对比轨迹LLM评判、纯文本LLM评判加红队、确定性启发式三类框架。三阶段实验发现：97%配置达稳定性阈值且与智能体无关；轨迹框架在72个已知风险用例上F1=0.90，纯文本召回相当但误报高5倍；未知风险发现24个新故障，功能与安全测试零重叠。研究表明评估信息量决定质量，两类评估互补，建议轨迹评估加对抗红队。
papers.abstract_en: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

papers.title_en: ToolTurns: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Dialogue
papers.authors: Milad Gholami, Brendan King, Jeffrey Flanigan
papers.evidence: 多轮对话中的LLM智能体基准
papers.tldr: 现有工具调用基准多聚焦孤立请求，难以衡量多轮对话中的澄清与上下文保持。作者提出 ToolTurns，含 2,620 道题、1,827 个工具和 11,004 个 API 端点，以欠指定初始请求加两次依赖上下文的追问评测智能体，并提供开源用户模拟器与 checker–fixer 改进对话质量。九款模型中最佳智能体单请求成功率达 69.6%，但完整对话仅 39.8%，且后续追问成功率普遍低于首轮。该基准揭示了多轮工具使用的能力缺口，并提供可复用的评测测试床。
papers.abstract_en: Tool-using language models are increasingly deployed in conversational settings, yet most large-scale tool-use benchmarks focus on isolated requests. We introduce ToolTurns, a benchmark of 2,620 problems spanning 1,827 tools and 11,004 API endpoints across 47 categories. Each dialogue begins with an intentionally underspecified request and continues through two context-dependent follow-ups, testing clarification, tool use, and retention of conversational context. We also introduce an open-source user simulator that reveals withheld context through dialogue and generates follow-up requests, with a checker--fixer pipeline for improving its turns. Across nine language models, the best agent resolves 69.6% of individual requests but completes only 39.8% of full dialogues. Under this evaluation protocol, every evaluated model receives lower success scores on follow-up requests than on the initial request, and dialogue-quality rubric scores and task success can rank models very differently. Paired turn-level evaluation shows that the checker--fixer reduces detected dialogue defects, and blind human evaluation favors the revised turns. ToolTurns provides a testbed for evaluating whether agents sustain task success across multi-turn dialogue with tools.

papers.title_en: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.authors: Jiali Cheng, Oleg Rokhlenko, Joo-Kyung Kim, Hadi Amiri, Xingzhi Guo
papers.evidence: 去中心化多智能体LLM协作基准
papers.tldr: 针对中心化多智能体系统依赖全局编排器带来的可扩展性与隐私问题，本文研究图约束通信下的去中心化协作：智能体仅见局部状态、只能与邻居交互。作者构建含10万+工具的分布式工具调用基准DecArena，发现现有LLM智能体难以发现非本地资源并协作，标准强化学习也难以可靠解决。为此提出GraphHarness，结合拓扑感知预热与自改进LLM路由，显著提升成功率与协作质量并降低成本。
papers.abstract_en: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting. Moreover, standard reinforcement learning fails to reliably overcome this limitation, suggesting that decentralized MAS needs more explicit harness mechanisms for effective collaboration, even using SOTA LLMs. We then present a strong baseline \textbf{GraphHarness}, combining topology-aware warmup with self-improving LLM-based routing. Results show that GraphHarness substantially improves task success (+48.5) and produces higher quality collaboration (+30.6), while using fewer costs (+34.0) than baselines.

papers.title_en: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
papers.authors: Yue Liu, Zhongying Ru, Shimin Di, Jipeng Zhang, Ruiyuan Zhang, Xiaofang Zhou
papers.evidence: 通过查询分解改进引用的可溯源RAG框架
papers.tldr: 可归因RAG需为答案生成引用，但现有多跳与多模态问题下易过度引用、隐式实体识别失败且泛化差。QDRAG将问题拆成原子子问题以识别隐式实体，并用重排器剪除干扰上下文；提出QD-C与QD-R两种零样本分解方法。四大多模态问答基准上，QDRAG在域内与域外均显著优于基线，甚至超过Gemini-Pro。实验还发现，直接微调问题分解任务比微调下游RAGQ任务更具泛化性。
papers.abstract_en: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation. To facilitate query decomposition, we propose two zero-shot approaches: QD-C and QD-R, which guide the QD MLLM to decompose the question based on context knowledge and retrieval rewards, respectively. One interesting finding is that finetuning on the QD task shows better generalizability compared to directly finetuning on the downstream RAGQ task. Experiments on four multi-modal QA benchmarks demonstrate QDRAG's efficacy in grounding answers and generating faithful citations. The framework significantly outperforms all the baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain tests, even surpassing Gemini-Pro.

papers.title_en: Does a Self-Learning Migration Agent Learn? An Audited Evaluation of Evidence-Graded Experience Memory for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
papers.authors: Oleg Grynets, Vasyl Lyashkevych, Valeriia Oliferuk, Vladyslav Babenko, Danylo Kovalchuk, Dmytro Kostetskyi
papers.evidence: 面向大模型智能体的证据分级持久经验记忆
papers.tldr: 论文追问LLM迁移智能体是否真能从经验学习，还是仅复用检索到的参考。作者在Oracle到PostgreSQL迁移中审计证据分级记忆，结合泄漏检查、复制基线、独立目标分组与行为验证。原始记忆仅提升参考符合度0.015，72%测试单元与训练共享参考，无泄漏后降至0.002；复制基线0.222反超所有LLM系统。真实PL/SQL中10-22%被PostgreSQL接受的结果行为错误，人工修复将正确单元从98/216提高到167/224，并提出六条评估规则。
papers.abstract_en: Do large language model (LLM) migration agents learn from accumulated experience, or do apparent gains reflect retrieval and reference reuse? We evaluate an evidence-graded agent for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration across four studies. On 1,833 documentation-derived source-reference pairs, persistent memory improved reference conformity (RC) over a no-memory baseline by 0.015 [0.004, 0.025], while policy adaptation added no gain (-0.004 [-0.010, 0.001]). An audit found that 264 of 367 held-out units (72%) shared a PostgreSQL reference with training, and the memory effect on the 103 leak-free units fell to 0.002 [-0.008, 0.011]. A model-free nearest-target copy baseline scored RC 0.222, outperforming all LLM systems (at most 0.163). A reference-grouped split reduced copying to 0.119; a rerun on 374 units in 118 independent target groups found no statistically distinguishable memory effect (0.005 [-0.003, 0.017]) and no policy effect. A separate Oracle-grounded evaluation on 216-224 real PL/SQL units showed that 10-22% of PostgreSQL-accepted units were behaviorally incorrect; a human-gated fix cycle increased demonstrably correct units from 98/216 to 167/224. A write-back study showed a 54% decline in retrieval margin as the knowledge base grew from 12 to 1,200 entries. We derive six evaluation rules that distinguish cross-task learning from reference leakage, copying, metric artifacts, and unstable feedback.

papers.title_en: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
papers.authors: Peiwen Li, Harshit Verma, Sophia Zhou, Haiwen Wang, Ngoc Bui, Heng Chang, Fei Fei, David van Dijk, Rex Ying
papers.evidence: 面向编码智能体的记忆选择与成本内化记忆
papers.tldr: 连续编码任务中，智能体需在未知下一任务前写入记忆，并权衡未来收益与读写成本。CoReMem 将记忆成本内生化，用前瞻分段估值筛选以仓库位置和可执行检查为锚的紧凑记忆，并做行动者适配。在 ChainSWE 上，27B 模型解决率由21.0%升至25.7%，步数减少17%，缓存感知总 token 减少11%。该工作为连续代码仓库任务提供了可测量的记忆价值框架。
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.

papers.title_en: MaRiO: Multi-agent Collaborative Reasoning via Shared Observations in MLLMs
papers.authors: Nathaniel Redmond, Fidel Omar Tito Cruz, Devansh Sharma, Shehreen Azad, Sirshapan Mitra, Shruti Vyas, Yogesh S. Rawat
papers.evidence: 多智能体协作推理评测基准
papers.tldr: 针对多智能体从独立视角观察共享环境、需跨观察协作推理却缺乏评测的问题，提出MaRiO基准并评测23个先进MLLM。进一步探索几何引导的合成视角增强，在智能体观察间生成中间过渡帧以提供空间上下文。结果显示静态感知任务较易，跨智能体对应与几何线索利用仍是主要瓶颈，增强仅部分类别有效。该工作揭示多智能体协作推理的开放挑战，为多模态具身系统提供评测与改进方向。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show strong visual perception capabilities, but existing evaluations largely focus on single-view or multi-view settings with shared camera parameters, leaving the challenge of multi-agent collaborative scenarios underexplored. In such settings, multiple agents observe a shared environment from independent viewpoints, and reliable decisions require reasoning across these independent observations of the same environment. To study this problem, we introduce MaRiO, a benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaborative reasoning, and evaluate 23 state-of-the-art MLLMs on it. Our analysis reveals three key findings: (1) tasks governed by static perception are generally easier than tasks that require transformational event sequences; (2) most models struggle to resolve cross-agent correspondences, with errors increasing with scene complexity; and (3) models show limited ability to leverage geometric cues present in the scene. As an initial step toward addressing these challenges, we explore geometry-guided synthetic view augmentation that generates intermediate transition frames between agent observations, providing auxiliary spatial context that improves performance in certain categories. Overall, our results highlight that multi-agent collaborative reasoning remains an open challenge and an important direction for multimodal embodied systems. The code is available on the project page: https://omarftt.github.io/MaRiO-page/.

papers.title_en: Replay Fidelity in LLM Agent Evaluation: Randomness, Hidden State, and Test Oracles in AppWorld
papers.evidence: 在 AppWorld 基准上审计大模型智能体评测的回放保真度
papers.tldr: LLM智能体评测的可复现性依赖回放保真度，即执行轨迹中哪些部分被重建、控制与比较。本文审计AppWorld固定历史语料中71次失败执行，开展284次固定代码隔离回放，并在每次交互前重置随机数生成器。结果显示声明设置仅容许42例，重置RNG后增至68例；数据库与判定检查使26例差距缩至4例，并发现输出和判定一致下的物化状态差异。研究刻画了回放资格、隐藏状态与测试预言集成，但未估计调试准确率或修复收益。
papers.abstract_en: Reproducibility in large language model (LLM) agent evaluation depends on replay fidelity: which parts of an execution trace are reconstructed, controlled, and compared. This matters for agent debugging, failure analysis, and counterfactual evaluation of stateful tool use. We audit all 71 unsuccessful executions in a fixed historical AppWorld corpus using 284 isolated fixed-code replay attempts. Reconstructed declared settings admit 42 cases under printed-output, pre-oracle database-delta, and native-verdict/test-count checks; resetting the random-number generator before each interaction admits 68. The 26-case gap contracts to four under database/oracle checks, with one endpoint unknown. Mechanism studies identify four materialized-state discrepancies despite matching outputs and verdicts. In one admitted endpoint pair, an identical API call yields matching responses but different row effects; common future Python RNG removes that deterministic difference in two paired repetitions. A separate JWT credential-equality program and alignment controls expose authentication/write differences, with missing repetitions retained. For all 10 affected post-oracle export cases, native export from retained output trackers restores the reference comparison without changing original cached contents. A purposeful 12-case BFCL pilot shows no discrepancy under its tested public-state, return, and verdict checks. We preserve resource censoring and infrastructure deviations. The contribution is a bounded empirical characterization of replay eligibility, hidden state, and test-oracle integration, without estimating debugger accuracy, repair gains, or method-ranking distortion.

papers.title_en: CURATOR: Scalable Fine-grained Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Decision Models
papers.authors: Shib Dasgupta, Bandish Parikh, Rashmi Gangadharaiah
papers.evidence: 面向检索增强生成的细粒度证据选择
papers.tldr: RAG通常把整段检索文本交给LLM，但真正相关证据只占少量片段，精确选择可提升上下文利用却受孤立判断与重复计算限制。CURATOR将证据选择建模为决策模型，并通过在大候选池中训练选择不同数量支持片段，实现高效联合决策。实验显示候选增多时仍保持强证据判别力，可跨任务与文档域泛化，并在上下文受限时提升下游RAG性能。
papers.abstract_en: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) provides entire retrieved passages to the LLM, even though only a handful of spans within them contain the evidence pertaining to the question. While precise selection of these spans can improve context utilization, identifying them in isolation is challenging. A span may appear irrelevant by itself, and deciding whether to retain it may require examining other retrieved information. One can evaluate each span's candidacy with the full retrieved context, but this is computationally inefficient as the same text must be processed repeatedly. Pretrained decision model can be used to efficiently evaluate multiple spans simultaneously, allowing each decision to consider the surrounding spans as well. However, our experiments show that their ability to identify relevant evidence deteriorates as the number of simultaneous decisions increases.   To address this, we introduce CURATOR, a fine-tuned decision model trained to make reliable evidence-selection decisions over large candidate sets. By training a decision model to select varying numbers of supporting spans from large candidate pools, CURATOR develops the capability to select evidence for RAG while retaining the computational efficiency of joint decision-making. We observe that CURATOR maintains a strong evidence discrimination capability as the number of candidates increases, generalizes across different tasks and document domains, and improves downstream RAG performance, particularly when the available context is limited.

papers.title_en: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
papers.authors: Saehun Chun, Wonje Choi, Jinwoo Jang, Taeyoon Kwack, Honguk Woo
papers.evidence: 面向具身智能体的异构记忆与KV复用
papers.tldr: 具身智能体需融合陈述性、程序性与工作记忆做决策，但现有异构记忆模块接口分离，记忆更新后常被当作全新输入，导致KV缓存无法选择性复用、重复计算开销大。HeMeR作为推理框架，跨动作决策跟踪三类记忆内容，保留未变内容的KV状态，仅对受记忆更新影响的KV状态进行协调。在ALFWorld、Habitat和真实机器人部署中验证，真实场景任务成功率达83.20%，单步推理从2.94秒降至1.87秒（对比MemRL）。该工作实现了记忆演化下的高效稳定推理，为异构记忆智能体提供结构化KV复用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. We introduce HeMeR, an inference framework that performs KV reconciliation between dynamically updated memory contexts and reusable KV states. HeMeR tracks declarative, procedural, and working memory contents across action decisions, preserves KV states for unchanged contents, and reconciles only the KV states affected by memory-content updates. This enables efficient and stable inference as memory contents evolve during interaction. We evaluate HeMeR on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robotic deployments requiring coordinated use of heterogeneous memory contents. In the real-world setting, HeMeR achieves 83.20% task success and reduces per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL, while preserving compatible KV states as task progress updates the memory context.
